entities.name: Walter Hungerford, 1st Baron Hungerford
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Walter Hungerford, 1st Baron Hungerford (d. 1449), emerged as a pivotal figure in early 15th-century England, navigating the complex political and military landscape under three successive Lancastrian monarchs: Henry IV, Henry V, and Henry VI. A distinguished knight, shrewd landowner, and astute politician, Hungerford's career spanned from the tumultuous end of the Hundred Years' War to the dawn of the Wars of the Roses, embodying the era's blend of martial prowess and administrative capability. His rise from a West Country gentry family to a peer of the realm, serving as Speaker of the House of Commons, Treasurer of England, and a key diplomat, underscores his significance in shaping English governance and foreign policy during a period of profound transition.

His military career was marked by active participation in the Hundred Years' War, most notably at the iconic Battle of Agincourt in 1415, where he served in Henry V's retinue and played a role in the English victory. Beyond the battlefield, Hungerford's influence grew through his parliamentary service, representing Wiltshire and other constituencies before being elected Speaker of the House of Commons in 1414. His administrative acumen was further recognized through his appointment as Steward of the Royal Household (1413–1422) and later as Treasurer of England (1426–1432), where he managed the Crown's often-strained finances. He also engaged in critical diplomatic missions, negotiating peace treaties with France and Scotland, thereby directly influencing England's international standing.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Walter Hungerford was a key figure in Lancastrian England, serving as Speaker of the House of Commons, Treasurer of England, and a distinguished military commander at Agincourt, thereby influencing English governance and foreign policy during a critical period of the Hundred Years' War. His establishment of the Barony of Hungerford secured a powerful aristocratic lineage in the West Country for generations.
